units.leftText: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the LORD’s word by Jeremiah’s mouth might be accomplished, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing, saying,
units.rightText: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, to fulfill the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah, the LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia to send a proclamation throughout his kingdom and to put it in writing as follows:
leftNotes: 1:1 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: “Cyrus king of Persia says, ‘The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he has commanded me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
units.rightText: “This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: ‘The LORD, the God of heaven, who has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, has appointed me to build a house for Him at Jerusalem in Judah.

units.leftText: Whoever there is among you of all his people, may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel (he is God), which is in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Whoever among you belongs to His people, may his God be with him, and may he go to Jerusalem in Judah and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel; He is the God who is in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Whoever is left, in any place where he lives, let the men of his place help him with silver, with gold, with goods, and with animals, in addition to the free will offering for God’s house which is in Jerusalem.’”
units.rightText: And let every survivor, wherever he lives, be assisted by the men of that region with silver, gold, goods, and livestock, along with a freewill offering for the house of God in Jerusalem.’”

units.leftText: Then the heads of fathers’ households of Judah and Benjamin, the priests and the Levites, all whose spirit God had stirred to go up, rose up to build the LORD’s house which is in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: So the family heads of Judah and Benjamin, along with the priests and Levites— everyone whose spirit God had stirred— prepared to go up and rebuild the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: All those who were around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, with animals, and with precious things, in addition to all that was willingly offered.
units.rightText: And all their neighbors supported them with articles of silver and gold, with goods and livestock, and with valuables, in addition to all their freewill offerings. Cyrus Restores the Holy Vessels

units.leftText: Also Cyrus the king brought out the vessels of the LORD’s house, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought out of Jerusalem, and had put in the house of his gods;
units.rightText: King Cyrus also brought out the articles belonging to the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem and placed in the temple of his gods.

units.leftText: even those, Cyrus king of Persia brought out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and counted them out to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah.
units.rightText: Cyrus king of Persia had them brought out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, who counted them out to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah.
rightNotes: 1:8 That is, the leader of the exiles returning to Judah

units.leftText: This is the number of them: thirty platters of gold, one thousand platters of silver, twenty-nine knives,
units.rightText: This was the inventory: 30 gold dishes, 1,000 silver dishes, 29 silver utensils,
rightNotes: 1:9 Or basins; twice in this verse

units.leftText: thirty bowls of gold, four hundred ten silver bowls of a second kind, and one thousand other vessels.
units.rightText: 30 gold bowls, 410 matching silver bowls, and 1,000 other articles.

units.leftText: All the vessels of gold and of silver were five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar brought all these up when the captives were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: In all, there were 5,400 gold and silver articles. Sheshbazzar brought all these along when the exiles went up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

units.rightText: Now these are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exiles carried away to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar its king. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town,

units.leftText: These sought their place among those who were registered by genealogy, but they were not found; therefore they were deemed disqualified and removed from the priesthood.
units.rightText: These men searched for their family records, but they could not find them and so were excluded from the priesthood as unclean.

units.leftText: The governor told them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest stood up to serve with Urim and with Thummim.
units.rightText: The governor ordered them not to eat the most holy things until there was a priest to consult the Urim and Thummim.

units.leftText: Some of the heads of fathers’ households, when they came to the LORD’s house which is in Jerusalem, offered willingly for God’s house to set it up in its place.
units.rightText: When they arrived at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, some of the heads of the families gave freewill offerings to rebuild the house of God on its original site.

units.leftText: They gave according to their ability into the treasury of the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold, five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priests’ garments.
units.rightText: According to their ability, they gave to the treasury for this work 61,000 darics of gold, 5,000 minas of silver, and 100 priestly garments.
leftNotes: 2:69 a daric was a gold coin issued by a Persian king, weighing about 8.4 grams or about 0.27 troy ounces each.
2:69 A mina is about 600 grams or 1.3 U. S. pounds, so 5,000 minas is about 3 metric tons.
rightNotes: 2:69 Or 61,000 gold drachmas; that is, approximately 1,129.7 pounds or 512.4 kilograms of gold coins
2:69 5,000 minas is approximately 3.14 tons or 2.85 metric tons of silver.

units.leftText: So the priests and the Levites, with some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants, lived in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.
units.rightText: So the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants, along with some of the people, settled in their own towns; and the rest of the Israelites settled in their towns.
rightNotes: 2:70 Or all Israel

units.leftText: When the seventh month had come, and the children of Israel were in the cities, the people gathered themselves together as one man to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: By the seventh month, the Israelites had settled in their towns, and the people assembled as one man in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Then Jeshua the son of Jozadak stood up with his brothers the priests and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and his relatives, and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the law of Moses the man of God.
units.rightText: Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, along with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his associates, began to build the altar of the God of Israel to sacrifice burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the Law of Moses the man of God.
rightNotes: 3:2 Jozadak is a variant of Jehozadak; also in verse 8; see 1 Chronicles 6:14|1CH 6:14*.

units.leftText: In spite of their fear because of the peoples of the surrounding lands, they set the altar on its base; and they offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD, even burnt offerings morning and evening.
units.rightText: They set up the altar on its foundation and sacrificed burnt offerings on it to the LORD — both the morning and evening burnt offerings — even though they feared the people of the land.

units.leftText: They kept the feast of booths, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the ordinance, as the duty of every day required;
units.rightText: They also celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles in accordance with what is written, and they offered burnt offerings daily based on the number prescribed for each day.
rightNotes: 3:4 That is, Sukkot, the autumn feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; also translated as the Feast of Booths or the Feast of Shelters and originally called the Feast of Ingathering(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16* and Exodus 34:22).

units.leftText: and afterward the continual burnt offering, the offerings of the new moons, of all the set feasts of the LORD that were consecrated, and of everyone who willingly offered a free will offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: After that, they presented the regular burnt offerings and those for New Moons and for all the appointed sacred feasts of the LORD, as well as all the freewill offerings brought to the LORD.

units.leftText: From the first day of the seventh month, they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD; but the foundation of the LORD’s temple was not yet laid.
units.rightText: On the first day of the seventh month, the Israelites began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, although the foundation of the temple of the LORD had not been laid.

units.leftText: They also gave money to the masons and to the carpenters. They also gave food, drink, and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar trees from Lebanon to the sea, to Joppa, according to the grant that they had from Cyrus King of Persia.
units.rightText: They gave money to the masons and carpenters, and food and drink and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar logs from Lebanon to Joppa by sea, as authorized by Cyrus king of Persia. Temple Restoration Begins

units.leftText: Now in the second year of their coming to God’s house at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and the rest of their brothers the priests and the Levites, and all those who had come out of the captivity to Jerusalem, began the work and appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to have the oversight of the work of the LORD’s house.
units.rightText: In the second month of the second year after they had arrived at the house of God in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, and the rest of their associates including the priests, the Levites, and all who had returned to Jerusalem from the captivity, began the work. They appointed Levites twenty years of age or older to supervise the construction of the house of the LORD.

units.leftText: Then Jeshua stood with his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, together to have the oversight of the workmen in God’s house: the sons of Henadad, with their sons and their brothers the Levites.
units.rightText: So Jeshua and his sons and brothers, Kadmiel and his sons (descendants of Yehudah), and the sons of Henadad and their sons and brothers — all Levites — joined together to supervise those working on the house of God.
rightNotes: 3:9 Hebrew sons of Judah; that is, most likely, sons of Yehudah, another name for Hodevah or Hodaviah; see Ezra 2:40|EZR 2:40* and Nehemiah 7:43.

units.leftText: When the builders laid the foundation of the LORD’s temple, they set the priests in their vestments with trumpets, with the Levites the sons of Asaph with cymbals, to praise the LORD, according to the directions of David king of Israel.
units.rightText: When the builders had laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, the priests in their apparel with trumpets, and the Levites (the sons of Asaph) with cymbals, took their positions to praise the LORD, as David king of Israel had prescribed.

units.leftText: They sang to one another in praising and giving thanks to the LORD, “For he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever toward Israel.” All the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised the LORD, because the foundation of the LORD’s house had been laid.
units.rightText: And they sang responsively with praise and thanksgiving to the LORD: “For He is good; for His loving devotion to Israel endures forever.” Then all the people gave a great shout of praise to the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid.
rightNotes: 3:11 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: But many of the priests and Levites and heads of fathers’ households, the old men who had seen the first house, when the foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, wept with a loud voice. Many also shouted aloud for joy,
units.rightText: But many of the older priests, Levites, and family heads who had seen the first temple wept loudly when they saw the foundation of this temple. Still, many others shouted joyfully.

units.leftText: so that the people could not discern the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people; for the people shouted with a loud shout, and the noise was heard far away.
units.rightText: The people could not distinguish the shouts of joy from the sound of weeping, because the people were making so much noise. And the sound was heard from afar.

units.leftText: Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity were building a temple to the LORD, the God of Israel,
units.rightText: When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the exiles were building a temple for the LORD, the God of Israel,

units.leftText: they came near to Zerubbabel, and to the heads of fathers’ households, and said to them, “Let us build with you, for we seek your God as you do; and we have been sacrificing to him since the days of Esar Haddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here.”
units.rightText: they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the families, saying, “Let us build with you because, like you, we seek your God and have been sacrificing to Him since the time of King Esar-haddon of Assyria, who brought us here.”

units.leftText: But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of fathers’ households of Israel said to them, “You have nothing to do with us in building a house to our God; but we ourselves together will build to the LORD, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus the king of Persia has commanded us.”
units.rightText: But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the other heads of the families of Israel replied, “You have no part with us in building a house for our God, since we alone must build it for the LORD, the God of Israel, as Cyrus king of Persia has commanded us.”

units.leftText: Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building.
units.rightText: Then the people of the land set out to discourage the people of Judah and make them afraid to build.

units.leftText: They hired counselors against them to frustrate their purpose all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
units.rightText: They hired counselors against them to frustrate their plans throughout the reign of Cyrus king of Persia and down to the reign of Darius king of Persia. Opposition under Xerxes and Artaxerxes

units.leftText: In the reign of Ahasuerus, in the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
units.rightText: At the beginning of the reign of Xerxes, an accusation was lodged against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
rightNotes: 4:6 Hebrew Ahasuerus

units.leftText: In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his companions wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia; and the writing of the letter was written in Syrian and delivered in the Syrian language.
units.rightText: And in the days of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his associates wrote a letter to Artaxerxes. It was written in Aramaic and then translated.
rightNotes: 4:7 The original text of Ezra 4:8|EZR 4:8* through Ezra 6:18 is in Aramaic.

units.leftText: Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king as follows.
units.rightText: Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote the letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes as follows:

units.leftText: Then Rehum the chancellor, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their companions, the Dinaites, and the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites, the Babylonians, the Shushanchites, the Dehaites, the Elamites,
units.rightText: From Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates— the judges and officials over Tripolis, Persia, Erech and Babylon, the Elamites of Susa,

units.leftText: and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Osnappar brought over and settled in the city of Samaria, and in the rest of the country beyond the River, and so forth, wrote.
units.rightText: and the rest of the peoples whom the great and honorable Ashurbanipal deported and settled in the cities of Samaria and elsewhere west of the Euphrates.
rightNotes: 4:10 Aramaic Osnappar, another name for Ashurbanipal
4:10 Aramaic beyond the River; also in verses 11, 16, 17, and 20

units.leftText: This is the copy of the letter that they sent: To King Artaxerxes, from your servants, the people beyond the River.
units.rightText: (This is the text of the letter they sent to him.) To King Artaxerxes, From your servants, the men west of the Euphrates:

units.leftText: Be it known to the king that the Jews who came up from you have come to us to Jerusalem. They are building the rebellious and bad city, and have finished the walls and repaired the foundations.
units.rightText: Let it be known to the king that the Jews who came from you to us have returned to Jerusalem and are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city. They are restoring its walls and repairing its foundations.

units.leftText: Be it known now to the king that if this city is built and the walls finished, they will not pay tribute, custom, or toll, and in the end it will be hurtful to the kings.
units.rightText: Let it now be known to the king that if that city is rebuilt and its walls are restored, they will not pay tribute, duty, or toll, and the royal treasury will suffer.

units.leftText: Now because we eat the salt of the palace and it is not appropriate for us to see the king’s dishonor, therefore we have sent and informed the king,
units.rightText: Now because we are in the service of the palace and it is not fitting for us to allow the king to be dishonored, we have sent to inform the king
rightNotes: 4:14 Literally because the salt of the palace is our salt

units.leftText: that search may be made in the book of the records of your fathers. You will see in the book of the records, and know that this city is a rebellious city, and hurtful to kings and provinces, and that they have started rebellions within it in the past. That is why this city was destroyed.
units.rightText: that a search should be made of the record books of your fathers. In these books you will discover and verify that the city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, inciting sedition from ancient times. That is why this city was destroyed.

units.leftText: We inform the king that if this city is built and the walls finished, then you will have no possession beyond the River.
units.rightText: We advise the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are restored, you will have no dominion west of the Euphrates. The Decree of Artaxerxes

units.leftText: Then the king sent an answer to Rehum the chancellor, and to Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest of their companions who live in Samaria, and in the rest of the country beyond the River: Peace.
units.rightText: Then the king sent this reply: To Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of your associates living in Samaria and elsewhere in the region west of the Euphrates: Greetings.

units.leftText: The letter which you sent to us has been plainly read before me.
units.rightText: The letter you sent us has been translated and read in my presence.

units.leftText: I decreed, and search has been made, and it was found that this city has made insurrection against kings in the past, and that rebellion and revolts have been made in it.
units.rightText: I issued a decree, and a search was conducted. It was discovered that this city has revolted against kings from ancient times, engaging in rebellion and sedition.

units.leftText: There have also been mighty kings over Jerusalem who have ruled over all the country beyond the River; and tribute, custom, and toll was paid to them.
units.rightText: And mighty kings have ruled over Jerusalem and exercised authority over the whole region west of the Euphrates; and tribute, duty, and toll were paid to them.

units.leftText: Make a decree now to cause these men to cease, and that this city not be built until a decree is made by me.
units.rightText: Now, therefore, issue an order for these men to stop, so that this city will not be rebuilt until I so order.

units.leftText: Be careful that you not be slack doing so. Why should damage grow to the hurt of the kings?
units.rightText: See that you do not neglect this matter. Why allow this threat to increase and the royal interests to suffer?

units.leftText: Then when the copy of King Artaxerxes’ letter was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their companions, they went in haste to Jerusalem to the Jews, and made them to cease by force of arms.
units.rightText: When the text of the letter from King Artaxerxes was read to Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates, they went immediately to the Jews in Jerusalem and forcibly stopped them.

units.leftText: Then work stopped on God’s house which is at Jerusalem. It stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
units.rightText: Thus the construction of the house of God in Jerusalem ceased, and it remained at a standstill until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.

units.leftText: Now the prophets, Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews who were in Judah and Jerusalem. They prophesied to them in the name of the God of Israel.
units.rightText: Later, the prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.

units.leftText: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak rose up and began to build God’s house which is at Jerusalem; and with them were the prophets of God, helping them.
units.rightText: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak rose up and began to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem. And the prophets of God were with them, helping them.
rightNotes: 5:2 Jozadak is a variant of Jehozadak; see 1 Chronicles 6:14|1CH 6:14*.

units.leftText: At the same time Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, came to them, with Shetharbozenai and their companions, and asked them, “Who gave you a decree to build this house and to finish this wall?”
units.rightText: At that time Tattenai the governor of the region west of the Euphrates, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates went to the Jews and asked, “Who authorized you to rebuild this temple and restore this structure?”
rightNotes: 5:3 Aramaic the governor beyond the River; also in verse 6

units.leftText: They also asked for the names of the men who were making this building.
units.rightText: They also asked, “What are the names of the men who are constructing this building?”
rightNotes: 5:4 LXX and Syriac; Aramaic Then we told them,

units.leftText: But the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, and they didn’t make them cease until the matter should come to Darius, and an answer should be returned by letter concerning it.
units.rightText: But the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, so that they were not stopped until a report was sent to Darius and written instructions about this matter were returned. Tattenai’s Letter to Darius

units.leftText: The copy of the letter that Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, and Shetharbozenai, and his companions the Apharsachites who were beyond the River, sent to Darius the king follows.
units.rightText: This is the text of the letter that Tattenai the governor of the region west of the Euphrates, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates, the officials in the region, sent to King Darius.

units.leftText: They sent a letter to him, in which was written: To Darius the king, all peace.
units.rightText: The report they sent him read as follows: To King Darius: All peace.

units.leftText: Be it known to the king that we went into the province of Judah, to the house of the great God, which is being built with great stones and timber is laid in the walls. This work goes on with diligence and prospers in their hands.
units.rightText: Let it be known to the king that we went into the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. The people are rebuilding it with large stones and placing timbers in the walls. This work is being carried out diligently and is prospering in their hands.

units.leftText: Then we asked those elders, and said to them thus, “Who gave you a decree to build this house, and to finish this wall?”
units.rightText: So we questioned the elders and asked, “Who authorized you to rebuild this temple and restore this structure?”

units.leftText: We asked them their names also, to inform you that we might write the names of the men who were at their head.
units.rightText: We also asked for their names, so that we could write down the names of their leaders for your information.
rightNotes: 5:10 Aramaic the names of the men at their heads

units.leftText: Thus they returned us answer, saying, “We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth and are building the house that was built these many years ago, which a great king of Israel built and finished.
units.rightText: And this is the answer they returned:

units.leftText: But after our fathers had provoked the God of heaven to wrath, he gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this house and carried the people away into Babylon.
units.rightText: But since our fathers angered the God of heaven, He delivered them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean who destroyed this temple and carried away the people to Babylon.

units.leftText: But in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, Cyrus the king made a decree to build this house of God.
units.rightText: In the first year of his reign, however, Cyrus king of Babylon issued a decree to rebuild this house of God.

units.leftText: The gold and silver vessels of God’s house, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the temple that was in Jerusalem and brought into the temple of Babylon, those Cyrus the king also took out of the temple of Babylon, and they were delivered to one whose name was Sheshbazzar, whom he had made governor.
units.rightText: He also removed from the temple of Babylon the gold and silver articles belonging to the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken and carried there from the temple in Jerusalem. King Cyrus gave these articles to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he appointed governor
rightNotes: 5:14 Or palace

units.leftText: He said to him, ‘Take these vessels, go, put them in the temple that is in Jerusalem, and let God’s house be built in its place.’
units.rightText: and instructed, ‘Take these articles, put them in the temple in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be rebuilt on its original site.’

units.leftText: Then the same Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of God’s house which is in Jerusalem. Since that time even until now it has been being built, and yet it is not completed.
units.rightText: So this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundation of the house of God in Jerusalem, and from that time until now it has been under construction, but it has not yet been completed.”

units.leftText: Now therefore, if it seems good to the king, let a search be made in the king’s treasure house, which is there at Babylon, whether it is so that a decree was made by Cyrus the king to build this house of God at Jerusalem; and let the king send his pleasure to us concerning this matter.”
units.rightText: Now, therefore, if it pleases the king, let a search be made of the royal archives in Babylon to see if King Cyrus did indeed issue a decree to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem. Then let the king send us his decision in this matter.

units.leftText: Then Darius the king made a decree, and the house of the archives, where the treasures were laid up in Babylon, was searched.
units.rightText: Thus King Darius ordered a search of the archives stored in the treasury of Babylon.

units.leftText: A scroll was found at Achmetha, in the palace that is in the province of Media, and in it this was written for a record:
units.rightText: And a scroll was found in the fortress of Ecbatana, in the province of Media, with the following written on it: Memorandum:

units.leftText: In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king made a decree: Concerning God’s house at Jerusalem, let the house be built, the place where they offer sacrifices, and let its foundations be strongly laid, with its height sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits;
units.rightText: In the first year of King Cyrus, he issued a decree concerning the house of God in Jerusalem:
leftNotes: 6:3 A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters.

units.leftText: with three courses of great stones and a course of new timber. Let the expenses be given out of the king’s house.
units.rightText: with three layers of cut stones and one of timbers. The costs are to be paid from the royal treasury.

units.leftText: Also let the gold and silver vessels of God’s house, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the temple which is at Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, be restored and brought again to the temple which is at Jerusalem, everything to its place. You shall put them in God’s house.
units.rightText: Furthermore, the gold and silver articles of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, must also be returned to the temple in Jerusalem and deposited in the house of God.

units.leftText: Now therefore, Tattenai, governor beyond the River, Shetharbozenai, and your companions the Apharsachites, who are beyond the River, you must stay far from there.
units.rightText: Therefore Darius decreed: To Tattenai governor of the region west of the Euphrates, Shethar-bozenai, and your associates and officials in the region:
rightNotes: 6:6 Aramaic governor beyond the River; similarly in verses 8 and 13

units.leftText: Leave the work of this house of God alone; let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build this house of God in its place.
units.rightText: Leave this work on the house of God alone. Let the governor and elders of the Jews rebuild this house of God on its original site.

units.leftText: Moreover I make a decree regarding what you shall do for these elders of the Jews for the building of this house of God: that of the king’s goods, even of the tribute beyond the River, expenses must be given with all diligence to these men, that they not be hindered.
units.rightText: I hereby decree what you must do for these elders of the Jews who are rebuilding this house of God:

units.leftText: That which they have need of, including young bulls, rams, and lambs, for burnt offerings to the God of heaven; also wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the word of the priests who are at Jerusalem, let it be given them day by day without fail,
units.rightText: Whatever is needed— young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and oil, as requested by the priests in Jerusalem— must be given to them daily without fail.

units.leftText: that they may offer sacrifices of pleasant aroma to the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king and of his sons.
units.rightText: Then they will be able to offer sacrifices of a sweet aroma to the God of heaven and to pray for the lives of the king and his sons.

units.leftText: I have also made a decree that whoever alters this message, let a beam be pulled out from his house, and let him be lifted up and fastened on it; and let his house be made a dunghill for this.
units.rightText: I also decree that if any man interferes with this directive, a beam is to be torn from his house and raised up, and he is to be impaled on it. And his own house shall be made a pile of rubble for this offense.
rightNotes: 6:11 Literally shall be made a dunghill because of this

units.leftText: May the God who has caused his name to dwell there overthrow all kings and peoples who stretch out their hand to alter this, to destroy this house of God which is at Jerusalem. I Darius have made a decree. Let it be done with all diligence.
units.rightText: May God, who has caused His Name to dwell there, overthrow any king or people who lifts a hand to alter this decree or to destroy this house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued the decree. Let it be carried out with diligence. The Temple Completed

units.leftText: Then Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, Shetharbozenai, and their companions did accordingly with all diligence, because Darius the king had sent a decree.
units.rightText: In response, Tattenai the governor of the region west of the Euphrates, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates diligently carried out what King Darius had decreed.

units.leftText: The elders of the Jews built and prospered, through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. They built and finished it, according to the commandment of the God of Israel, and according to the decree of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
units.rightText: So the Jewish elders built and prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo.

units.leftText: This house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.
units.rightText: And this temple was completed on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius. Dedication of the Temple
rightNotes: 6:15 Adar is the twelfth month of the Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of February and March.

units.leftText: The children of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication of this house of God with joy.
units.rightText: Then the people of Israel — the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the exiles — celebrated the dedication of the house of God with joy.

units.leftText: They offered at the dedication of this house of God one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and for a sin offering for all Israel, twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
units.rightText: For the dedication of the house of God they offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and a sin offering for all Israel of twelve male goats, one for each tribe of Israel.

units.leftText: They set the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their courses, for the service of God which is at Jerusalem, as it is written in the book of Moses.
units.rightText: They also appointed the priests by their divisions and the Levites by their groups to the service of God in Jerusalem, according to what is written in the Book of Moses. The Returned Exiles Keep the Passover

units.leftText: The children of the captivity kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
units.rightText: On the fourteenth day of the first month, the exiles kept the Passover.

units.leftText: Because the priests and the Levites had purified themselves together, all of them were pure. They killed the Passover for all the children of the captivity, for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.
units.rightText: All the priests and Levites had purified themselves and were ceremonially clean.

units.leftText: The children of Israel who had returned out of the captivity, and all who had separated themselves to them from the filthiness of the nations of the land to seek the LORD, the God of Israel, ate,
units.rightText: The Israelites who had returned from exile ate it, together with all who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the peoples of the land to seek the LORD, the God of Israel.
rightNotes: 6:21 Or nations

units.leftText: and kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy; because the LORD had made them joyful, and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria to them, to strengthen their hands in the work of God, the God of Israel’s house.
units.rightText: For seven days they kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread with joy, because the LORD had made them joyful and turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them to strengthen their hands in the work on the house of the God of Israel.
rightNotes: 6:22 That is, the seven-day period after the Passover during which no leaven may be eaten; see Exodus 12:14–20|EXO 12:14-20*.

units.leftText: Now after these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra the son of Seraiah, the son of Azariah, the son of Hilkiah,
units.rightText: Many years later, during the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra son of Seraiah, the son of Azariah, the son of Hilkiah,
rightNotes: 7:1 Literally After these things

units.leftText: the son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub,
units.rightText: the son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub,

units.leftText: the son of Amariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth,
units.rightText: the son of Amariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth,

units.leftText: the son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki,
units.rightText: the son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki,

units.leftText: the son of Abishua, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the chief priest—
units.rightText: the son of Abishua, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the chief priest—

units.leftText: this Ezra went up from Babylon. He was a skilled scribe in the law of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given; and the king granted him all his request, according to the LORD his God’s hand on him.
units.rightText: this Ezra came up from Babylon. He was a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given.

units.leftText: Some of the children of Israel, including some of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.
units.rightText: So in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes, he went up to Jerusalem with some of the Israelites, including priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants.
rightNotes: 7:7 Hebrew Nethinim; also in verse 24

units.leftText: He came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was in the seventh year of the king.
units.rightText: Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of the seventh year of the king.

units.leftText: For on the first day of the first month he began to go up from Babylon; and on the first day of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God on him.
units.rightText: He had begun the journey from Babylon on the first day of the first month, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, for the gracious hand of his God was upon him.

units.leftText: For Ezra had set his heart to seek the LORD’s law, and to do it, and to teach statutes and ordinances in Israel.
units.rightText: For Ezra had set his heart to study the Law of the LORD, to practice it, and to teach its statutes and ordinances in Israel. Artaxerxes’ Letter for Ezra

units.leftText: Now this is the copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe, even the scribe of the words of the LORD’s commandments, and of his statutes to Israel:
units.rightText: This is the text of the letter King Artaxerxes had given to Ezra the priest and scribe, an expert in the commandments and statutes of the LORD to Israel:
rightNotes: 7:11 The original text of Ezra 7:12–26|EZR 7:12-26* is in Aramaic.

units.leftText: Artaxerxes, king of kings, To Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the perfect God of heaven. Now
units.rightText: Artaxerxes, king of kings. To Ezra the priest, the scribe of the Law of the God of heaven: Greetings.
rightNotes: 7:12 Aramaic Perfect now (probably a greeting)

units.leftText: I make a decree that all those of the people of Israel and their priests and the Levites in my realm, who intend of their own free will to go to Jerusalem, go with you.
units.rightText: I hereby decree that any volunteers among the Israelites in my kingdom, including the priests and Levites, may go up with you to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Because you are sent by the king and his seven counselors to inquire concerning Judah and Jerusalem, according to the law of your God which is in your hand,
units.rightText: You are sent by the king and his seven counselors to evaluate Judah and Jerusalem according to the Law of your God, which is in your hand.

units.leftText: and to carry the silver and gold, which the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose habitation is in Jerusalem,
units.rightText: Moreover, you are to take with you the silver and gold that the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,

units.leftText: and all the silver and gold that you will find in all the province of Babylon, with the free will offering of the people and of the priests, offering willingly for the house of their God which is in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: together with all the silver and gold you may find in all the province of Babylon, as well as the freewill offerings of the people and priests to the house of their God in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Therefore you shall with all diligence buy with this money bulls, rams, and lambs with their meal offerings and their drink offerings, and shall offer them on the altar of the house of your God which is in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: With this money, therefore, you are to buy as many bulls, rams, and lambs as needed, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and offer them on the altar at the house of your God in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Whatever seems good to you and to your brothers to do with the rest of the silver and the gold, do that according to the will of your God.
units.rightText: You and your brothers may do whatever seems best with the rest of the silver and gold, according to the will of your God.

units.leftText: The vessels that are given to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver before the God of Jerusalem.
units.rightText: You must deliver to the God of Jerusalem all the articles given to you for the service of the house of your God.

units.leftText: Whatever more will be needed for the house of your God, which you may have occasion to give, give it out of the king’s treasure house.
units.rightText: And if anything else is needed for the house of your God that you may have occasion to supply, you may pay for it from the royal treasury.

units.leftText: I, even I, Artaxerxes the king, make a decree to all the treasurers who are beyond the River, that whatever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, requires of you, it shall be done with all diligence,
units.rightText: I, King Artaxerxes, decree to all the treasurers west of the Euphrates: Whatever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the Law of the God of heaven, may require of you, it must be provided promptly,
rightNotes: 7:21 Aramaic beyond the River; also in verse 25

units.leftText: up to one hundred talents of silver, and to one hundred cors of wheat, and to one hundred baths of wine, and to one hundred baths of oil, and salt without prescribing how much.
units.rightText: up to a hundred talents of silver, a hundred cors of wheat, a hundred baths of wine, a hundred baths of olive oil, and salt without limit.
leftNotes: 7:22 A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds or 965 Troy ounces
7:22 1 cor is the same as a homer, or about 55.9 U. S. gallons (liquid) or 211 liters or 6 bushels.
7:22 1 bath is one tenth of a cor, or about 5.6 U. S. gallons or 21 liters or 2.4 pecks. 100 baths would be about 2,100 liters.
rightNotes: 7:22 100 talents is approximately 3.77 tons or 3.42 metric tons of silver.
7:22 100 cors is approximately 624 bushels or 22,000 liters (probably about 19.2 tons or 17.4 metric tons of wheat).
7:22 100 baths is approximately 580 gallons or 2,200 liters of wine.
7:22 Or 100 baths of oil; that is, approximately 580 gallons or 2,200 liters

units.leftText: Whatever is commanded by the God of heaven, let it be done exactly for the house of the God of heaven; for why should there be wrath against the realm of the king and his sons?
units.rightText: Whatever is commanded by the God of heaven must be done diligently for His house. For why should wrath fall on the realm of the king and his sons?

units.leftText: Also we inform you that it shall not be lawful to impose tribute, custom, or toll on any of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants, or laborers of this house of God.
units.rightText: And be advised that you have no authority to impose tribute, duty, or toll on any of the priests, Levites, singers, doorkeepers, temple servants, or other servants of this house of God.

units.leftText: You, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God that is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges who may judge all the people who are beyond the River, who all know the laws of your God; and teach him who doesn’t know them.
units.rightText: And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God, which you possess, are to appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people west of the Euphrates — all who know the laws of your God. And you are to teach these laws to anyone who does not know them.

units.leftText: Whoever will not do the law of your God and the law of the king, let judgment be executed on him with all diligence, whether it is to death, or to banishment, or to confiscation of goods, or to imprisonment.
units.rightText: If anyone does not keep the law of your God and the law of the king, let a strict judgment be executed against him, whether death, banishment, confiscation of property, or imprisonment. Ezra Blesses God

units.leftText: Blessed be the LORD, the God of our fathers, who has put such a thing as this in the king’s heart, to beautify the LORD’s house which is in Jerusalem;
units.rightText: Blessed be the LORD, the God of our fathers, who has put into the heart of the king to so honor the house of the LORD in Jerusalem,

units.leftText: and has extended loving kindness to me before the king and his counselors, and before all the king’s mighty princes. I was strengthened according to the LORD my God’s hand on me, and I gathered together chief men out of Israel to go up with me.
units.rightText: and who has shown me favor before the king, his counselors, and all his powerful officials. And because the hand of the LORD my God was upon me, I took courage and gathered the leaders of Israel to return with me.

units.leftText: Now these are the heads of their fathers’ households, and this is the genealogy of those who went up with me from Babylon, in the reign of Artaxerxes the king:
units.rightText: These are the family heads and genealogical records of those who returned with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes:

units.leftText: Of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom. Of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel. Of the sons of David, Hattush.
units.rightText: from the descendants of Phinehas, Gershom; from the descendants of Ithamar, Daniel;

units.leftText: Of the sons of Shecaniah, of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah; and with him were listed by genealogy of the males one hundred fifty.
units.rightText: of the descendants of Shecaniah; from the descendants of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him were registered 150 men;

units.leftText: Of the sons of Pahathmoab, Eliehoenai the son of Zerahiah; and with him two hundred males.
units.rightText: from the descendants of Pahath-Moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him 200 men;

units.leftText: Of the sons of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel; and with him three hundred males.
units.rightText: from the descendants of Zattu, Shecaniah son of Jahaziel, and with him 300 men;
rightNotes: 8:5 Some LXX manuscripts (see also 1 Esdras 8:32|8:32*); Hebrew from the descendants of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel

units.leftText: Of the sons of Adin, Ebed the son of Jonathan; and with him fifty males.
units.rightText: from the descendants of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him 50 men;

units.leftText: Of the sons of Elam, Jeshaiah the son of Athaliah; and with him seventy males.
units.rightText: from the descendants of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him 70 men;

units.leftText: Of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah the son of Michael; and with him eighty males.
units.rightText: from the descendants of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him 80 men;

units.leftText: Of the sons of Joab, Obadiah the son of Jehiel; and with him two hundred eighteen males.
units.rightText: from the descendants of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him 218 men;

units.leftText: Of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah; and with him one hundred sixty males.
units.rightText: from the descendants of Bani, Shelomith son of Josiphiah, and with him 160 men;
rightNotes: 8:10 Some LXX manuscripts (see also 1 Esdras 8:36|8:36*); Hebrew from the descendants of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah

units.leftText: Of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah the son of Bebai; and with him twenty-eight males.
units.rightText: from the descendants of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him 28 men;

units.leftText: Of the sons of Azgad, Johanan the son of Hakkatan; and with him one hundred ten males.
units.rightText: from the descendants of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him 110 men;

units.leftText: Of the sons of Adonikam, who were the last, their names are: Eliphelet, Jeuel, and Shemaiah; and with them sixty males.
units.rightText: from the later descendants of Adonikam, these were their names: Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, and with them 60 men;
rightNotes: 8:13 Or the last

units.leftText: Of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zabbud; and with them seventy males.
units.rightText: and from the descendants of Bigvai, both Uthai and Zaccur, and with them 70 men. Ezra Sends for the Levites
rightNotes: 8:14 LXX, Syriac, and an alternate MT reading; the other alternate reads Zabbud.

units.leftText: I gathered them together to the river that runs to Ahava; and there we encamped three days. Then I looked around at the people and the priests, and found there were none of the sons of Levi.
units.rightText: Now I assembled these exiles at the canal that flows to Ahava, and we camped there three days. And when I searched among the people and priests, I found no Levites there.

units.leftText: Then I sent for Eliezer, for Ariel, for Shemaiah, for Elnathan, for Jarib, for Elnathan, for Nathan, for Zechariah, and for Meshullam, chief men; also for Joiarib and for Elnathan, who were teachers.
units.rightText: Then I summoned the leaders: Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, as well as the teachers Joiarib and Elnathan.
rightNotes: 8:16 Elnathan appears three times in verse, either as a repetition for emphasis or as a record of multiple men with this name.

units.leftText: I sent them out to Iddo the chief at the place Casiphia; and I told them what they should tell Iddo and his brothers the temple servants at the place Casiphia, that they should bring to us ministers for the house of our God.
units.rightText: And I sent them to Iddo, the leader at Casiphia, with a message for him and his kinsmen, the temple servants at Casiphia, that they should bring to us ministers for the house of our God.
rightNotes: 8:17 Hebrew the Nethinim; also in verse 20

units.leftText: According to the good hand of our God on us they brought us a man of discretion, of the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel, namely Sherebiah, with his sons and his brothers, eighteen;
units.rightText: And since the gracious hand of our God was upon us, they brought us Sherebiah— a man of insight from the descendants of Mahli son of Levi, the son of Israel— along with his sons and brothers, 18 men;

units.leftText: and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, his brothers and their sons, twenty;
units.rightText: also Hashabiah, together with Jeshaiah, from the descendants of Merari, and his brothers and their sons, 20 men.

units.leftText: and of the temple servants, whom David and the princes had given for the service of the Levites, two hundred twenty temple servants. All of them were mentioned by name.
units.rightText: They also brought 220 of the temple servants, all designated by name. David and the officials had appointed them to assist the Levites. Fasting for Protection

units.leftText: Then I proclaimed a fast there at the river Ahava, that we might humble ourselves before our God, to seek from him a straight way for us, for our little ones, and for all our possessions.
units.rightText: And there by the Ahava Canal I proclaimed a fast, so that we might humble ourselves before our God and ask Him for a safe journey for us and our children, with all our possessions.

units.leftText: For I was ashamed to ask of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help us against the enemy on the way, because we had spoken to the king, saying, “The hand of our God is on all those who seek him, for good; but his power and his wrath is against all those who forsake him.”
units.rightText: For I was ashamed to ask the king for an escort of soldiers and horsemen to protect us from our enemies on the road, since we had told him, “The hand of our God is gracious to all who seek Him, but His great anger is against all who forsake Him.”

units.leftText: So we fasted and begged our God for this, and he granted our request.
units.rightText: So we fasted and petitioned our God about this, and He granted our request. Priests to Guard the Offerings

units.leftText: Then I set apart twelve of the chiefs of the priests, even Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers with them,
units.rightText: Then I set apart twelve of the leading priests, together with Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers,

units.leftText: and weighed to them the silver, the gold, and the vessels, even the offering for the house of our God, which the king, his counselors, his princes, and all Israel there present, had offered.
units.rightText: and I weighed out to them the contribution of silver and gold and the articles that the king, his counselors, his leaders, and all the Israelites there had offered for the house of our God.

units.leftText: I weighed into their hand six hundred fifty talents of silver, one hundred talents of silver vessels, one hundred talents of gold,
units.rightText: I weighed out into their hands 650 talents of silver, articles of silver weighing 100 talents, 100 talents of gold,
leftNotes: 8:26 A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds or 965 Troy ounces
rightNotes: 8:26 650 talents is approximately 24.5 tons or 22.2 metric tons of silver.
8:26 100 talents is approximately 3.77 tons or 3.42 metric tons of silver articles.
8:26 100 talents is approximately 3.77 tons or 3.42 metric tons of gold.

units.leftText: twenty bowls of gold weighing one thousand darics, and two vessels of fine bright bronze, precious as gold.
units.rightText: 20 gold bowls valued at 1,000 darics, and two articles of fine polished bronze, as precious as gold.
leftNotes: 8:27 a daric was a gold coin issued by a Persian king, weighing about 8.4 grams or about 0.27 troy ounces each.
rightNotes: 8:27 Or worth 1,000 drachmas; that is, approximately 18.5 pounds or 8.4 kilograms of gold

units.leftText: I said to them, “You are holy to the LORD, and the vessels are holy. The silver and the gold are a free will offering to the LORD, the God of your fathers.
units.rightText: Then I told them, “You are holy to the LORD, and these articles are holy. The silver and gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your fathers.

units.leftText: Watch and keep them until you weigh them before the chiefs of the priests, the Levites, and the princes of the fathers’ households of Israel at Jerusalem, in the rooms of the LORD’s house.”
units.rightText: Guard them carefully until you weigh them out in the chambers of the house of the LORD in Jerusalem before the leading priests, Levites, and heads of the Israelite families.”

units.leftText: So the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver, the gold, and the vessels, to bring them to Jerusalem to the house of our God.
units.rightText: So the priests and Levites took charge of the silver and gold and sacred articles that had been weighed out to be taken to the house of our God in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Then we departed from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month, to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was on us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy and the bandits by the way.
units.rightText: On the twelfth day of the first month we set out from the Ahava Canal to go to Jerusalem, and the hand of our God was upon us to protect us from the hands of the enemies and bandits along the way. Arrival in Jerusalem

units.leftText: We came to Jerusalem, and stayed there three days.
units.rightText: So we arrived at Jerusalem and rested there for three days.

units.leftText: On the fourth day the silver and the gold and the vessels were weighed in the house of our God into the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest; and with him was Eleazar the son of Phinehas; and with them were Jozabad the son of Jeshua, and Noadiah the son of Binnui, the Levites.
units.rightText: On the fourth day, in the house of our God, we weighed out the silver and gold and sacred articles into the hand of Meremoth son of Uriah, the priest. Eleazar son of Phinehas was with him, along with the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.

units.leftText: Everything was counted and weighed; and all the weight was written at that time.
units.rightText: Everything was verified by number and weight, and the total weight was recorded at that time.

units.leftText: The children of the captivity, who had come out of exile, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats for a sin offering. All this was a burnt offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: Then the exiles who had returned from captivity sacrificed burnt offerings to the God of Israel: 12 bulls for all Israel, 96 rams, 77 lambs, and a sin offering of 12 male goats. All this was a burnt offering to the LORD.

units.leftText: They delivered the king’s commissions to the king’s local governors and to the governors beyond the River. So they supported the people and God’s house.
units.rightText: They also delivered the king’s edicts to the royal satraps and governors of the region west of the Euphrates, who proceeded to assist the people and the house of God.
rightNotes: 8:36 A satrap was a Persian official.
8:36 Hebrew governors beyond the River

units.leftText: Now when these things were done, the princes came near to me, saying, “The people of Israel, the priests, and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands, following their abominations, even those of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.
units.rightText: After these things had been accomplished, the leaders approached me and said, “The people of Israel, including the priests and Levites, have not kept themselves separate from the surrounding peoples whose abominations are like those of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.

units.leftText: For they have taken of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, so that the holy offspring have mixed themselves with the peoples of the lands. Yes, the hand of the princes and rulers has been chief in this trespass.”
units.rightText: Indeed, the Israelites have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons, so that the holy seed has been mixed with the people of the land. And the leaders and officials have taken the lead in this unfaithfulness!”

units.leftText: When I heard this thing, I tore my garment and my robe, and pulled the hair out of my head and of my beard, and sat down confounded.
units.rightText: When I heard this report, I tore my tunic and cloak, pulled out some hair from my head and beard, and sat down in horror.

units.leftText: Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel were assembled to me because of the trespass of the exiles; and I sat confounded until the evening offering.
units.rightText: Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles, while I sat there in horror until the evening offering. Ezra’s Prayer of Confession

units.leftText: At the evening offering I rose up from my humiliation, even with my garment and my robe torn; and I fell on my knees, and spread out my hands to the LORD my God;
units.rightText: At the evening offering, I got up from my humiliation with my tunic and cloak torn, and I fell on my knees, spread out my hands to the LORD my God,

units.leftText: and I said, “My God, I am ashamed and blush to lift up my face to you, my God, for our iniquities have increased over our head, and our guiltiness has grown up to the heavens.
units.rightText: and said:

units.leftText: Since the days of our fathers we have been exceedingly guilty to this day; and for our iniquities we, our kings, and our priests have been delivered into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to confusion of face, as it is this day.
units.rightText: From the days of our fathers to this day, our guilt has been great. Because of our iniquities, we and our kings and priests have been delivered into the hands of the kings of the earth and subjected to the sword and to captivity, to pillage and humiliation, as we are this day.

units.leftText: Now for a little moment grace has been shown from the LORD our God, to leave us a remnant to escape, and to give us a stake in his holy place, that our God may lighten our eyes, and revive us a little in our bondage.
units.rightText: But now, for a brief moment, grace has come from the LORD our God to preserve for us a remnant and to give us a stake in His holy place. Even in our bondage, our God has given us new life and light to our eyes.
rightNotes: 9:8 Or nail or foothold

units.leftText: For we are bondservants; yet our God has not forsaken us in our bondage, but has extended loving kindness to us in the sight of the kings of Persia, to revive us, to set up the house of our God, and to repair its ruins, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Though we are slaves, our God has not forsaken us in our bondage, but He has extended to us grace in the sight of the kings of Persia, giving us new life to rebuild the house of our God and repair its ruins, and giving us a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem.

units.leftText: “Now, our God, what shall we say after this? For we have forsaken your commandments,
units.rightText: And now, our God, what can we say after this? For we have forsaken the commandments

units.leftText: which you have commanded by your servants the prophets, saying, ‘The land to which you go to possess is an unclean land through the uncleanness of the peoples of the lands, through their abominations, which have filled it from one end to another with their filthiness.
units.rightText: that You gave through Your servants the prophets, saying: ‘The land that you are entering to possess is a land polluted by the impurity of its peoples and the abominations with which they have filled it from end to end.

units.leftText: Now therefore don’t give your daughters to their sons. Don’t take their daughters to your sons, nor seek their peace or their prosperity forever, that you may be strong and eat the good of the land, and leave it for an inheritance to your children forever.’
units.rightText: Now, therefore, do not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters for your sons. Never seek their peace or prosperity, so that you may be strong and may eat the good things of the land, leaving it as an inheritance to your sons forever.’

units.leftText: “After all that has come on us for our evil deeds and for our great guilt, since you, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and have given us such a remnant,
units.rightText: After all that has come upon us because of our evil deeds and our great guilt (though You, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities deserve and have given us such a remnant as this),

units.leftText: shall we again break your commandments, and join ourselves with the peoples that do these abominations? Wouldn’t you be angry with us until you had consumed us, so that there would be no remnant, nor any to escape?
units.rightText: shall we again break Your commandments and intermarry with the peoples who commit these abominations? Would You not become so angry with us as to wipe us out, leaving no remnant or survivor?

units.leftText: LORD, the God of Israel, you are righteous; for we are left a remnant that has escaped, as it is today. Behold, we are before you in our guiltiness; for no one can stand before you because of this.”
units.rightText: O LORD, God of Israel, You are righteous! For we remain this day as a remnant. Here we are before You in our guilt, though because of it no one can stand before You.”
leftNotes: 9:15 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: Now while Ezra prayed and made confession, weeping and casting himself down before God’s house, there was gathered together to him out of Israel a very great assembly of men and women and children; for the people wept very bitterly.
units.rightText: While Ezra prayed and made this confession, weeping and falling facedown before the house of God, a very large assembly of Israelites — men, women, and children — gathered around him, and the people wept bitterly as well.

units.leftText: Shecaniah the son of Jehiel, one of the sons of Elam, answered Ezra, “We have trespassed against our God, and have married foreign women of the peoples of the land. Yet now there is hope for Israel concerning this thing.
units.rightText: Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, an Elamite, said to Ezra: “We have been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women from the people of the land, yet in spite of this, there is hope for Israel.

units.leftText: Now therefore let’s make a covenant with our God to put away all the wives and those who are born of them, according to the counsel of my lord and of those who tremble at the commandment of our God. Let it be done according to the law.
units.rightText: So now let us make a covenant before our God to send away all the foreign wives and their children, according to the counsel of my lord and of those who tremble at the command of our God. Let it be done according to the Law.

units.leftText: Arise, for the matter belongs to you and we are with you. Be courageous, and do it.”
units.rightText: Get up, for this matter is your responsibility, and we will support you. Be strong and take action!”

units.leftText: Then Ezra arose, and made the chiefs of the priests, the Levites, and all Israel to swear that they would do according to this word. So they swore.
units.rightText: So Ezra got up and made the leading priests, Levites, and all Israel take an oath to do what had been said. And they took the oath. The People’s Confession of Sin

units.leftText: Then Ezra rose up from before God’s house, and went into the room of Jehohanan the son of Eliashib. When he came there, he didn’t eat bread or drink water, for he mourned because of the trespass of the exiles.
units.rightText: Then Ezra withdrew from before the house of God and walked to the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. And while he stayed there, he ate no food and drank no water, because he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exiles.
rightNotes: 10:6 Or went

units.leftText: They made a proclamation throughout Judah and Jerusalem to all the children of the captivity, that they should gather themselves together to Jerusalem;
units.rightText: And a proclamation was issued throughout Judah and Jerusalem that all the exiles should gather at Jerusalem.

units.leftText: and that whoever didn’t come within three days, according to the counsel of the princes and the elders, all his possessions should be forfeited, and he himself separated from the assembly of the captivity.
units.rightText: Whoever failed to appear within three days would forfeit all his property, according to the counsel of the leaders and elders, and would himself be expelled from the assembly of the exiles.

units.leftText: Then all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered themselves together to Jerusalem within the three days. It was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month; and all the people sat in the wide place in front of God’s house, trembling because of this matter, and because of the great rain.
units.rightText: So within the three days, all the men of Judah and Benjamin assembled in Jerusalem, and on the twentieth day of the ninth month, all the people sat in the square at the house of God, trembling regarding this matter and because of the heavy rain.

units.leftText: Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, “You have trespassed, and have married foreign women, increasing the guilt of Israel.
units.rightText: Then Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, “You have been unfaithful by marrying foreign women, adding to the guilt of Israel.

units.leftText: Now therefore make confession to the LORD, the God of your fathers and do his pleasure. Separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign women.”
units.rightText: Now, therefore, make a confession to the LORD, the God of your fathers, and do His will. Separate yourselves from the people of the land and from your foreign wives.”

units.leftText: Then all the assembly answered with a loud voice, “We must do as you have said concerning us.
units.rightText: And the whole assembly responded in a loud voice: “Truly we must do as you say!

units.leftText: But the people are many, and it is a time of much rain, and we are not able to stand outside. This is not a work of one day or two, for we have greatly transgressed in this matter.
units.rightText: But there are many people here, and it is the rainy season. We are not able to stay out in the open. Nor is this the work of one or two days, for we have transgressed greatly in this matter.

units.leftText: Now let our princes be appointed for all the assembly, and let all those who are in our cities who have married foreign women come at appointed times, and with them the elders of every city and its judges, until the fierce wrath of our God is turned from us, until this matter is resolved.”
units.rightText: Let our leaders represent the whole assembly. Then let everyone in our towns who has married a foreign woman come at an appointed time, together with the elders and judges of each town, until the fierce anger of our God in this matter is turned away from us.”

units.leftText: Only Jonathan the son of Asahel and Jahzeiah the son of Tikvah stood up against this; and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them.
units.rightText: (Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah, supported by Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite, opposed this plan.)

units.leftText: The children of the captivity did so. Ezra the priest, with certain heads of fathers’ households, after their fathers’ houses, and all of them by their names, were set apart; and they sat down in the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter.
units.rightText: So the exiles did as proposed. Ezra the priest selected men who were family heads, each of them identified by name, to represent their families. On the first day of the tenth month they launched the investigation,

units.leftText: They finished with all the men who had married foreign women by the first day of the first month.
units.rightText: and by the first day of the first month they had dealt with all the men who had married foreign women. Those Guilty of Intermarriage

units.leftText: Among the sons of the priests there were found who had married foreign women: of the sons of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and his brothers: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.
units.rightText: Among the descendants of the priests who had married foreign women were found these descendants of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers:
rightNotes: 10:18 Jozadak is a variant of Jehozadak; see 1 Chronicles 6:14|1CH 6:14*.

units.leftText: They gave their hand that they would put away their wives; and being guilty, they offered a ram of the flock for their guilt.
units.rightText: They pledged to send their wives away, and for their guilt they presented a ram from the flock as a guilt offering.

units.rightText: From the descendants of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.

units.rightText: From the descendants of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.

units.leftText: Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.
units.rightText: Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.

units.leftText: Of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Iddo, Joel, and Benaiah.
units.rightText: And from the descendants of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.

units.leftText: All these had taken foreign wives. Some of them had wives by whom they had children.
units.rightText: All these men had married foreign women, and some of them had children by these wives.
rightNotes: 10:44 Or and they sent them away with their children
